title: Protecting Your Eyes
hook: Some of the most serious eye diseases, like glaucoma, steal sight silently with no early symptoms. A regular eye exam is often the only way to catch them in time.
key_points: Comprehensive eye exams can catch silent diseases like glaucoma before vision is lost.
Wear sunglasses that block UV to lower long-term risk to your eyes.
Ease screen strain with the 20-20-20 habit: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Diabetes can damage the eyes, so people with it need regular dilated exams.
Sudden vision changes or eye pain warrant prompt medical attention.
content_html: We tend to ignore our eyes until something goes wrong, but several of the diseases that cause permanent vision loss — glaucoma chief among them — give no warning signs early on. That's why routine eye care matters even when your sight feels perfectly fine.
extra_html: The National Eye Institute recommends comprehensive dilated eye exams as the best way to catch problems early, since conditions like glaucoma can progress silently until vision is already damaged. A few everyday habits help too: wearing sunglasses that block ultraviolet light protects the eyes over the long term, and giving your eyes regular breaks from screens — for example, the 20-20-20 approach of looking 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes — eases digital strain. Diabetes is a notable risk to vision, so people living with it need regular dilated exams to catch damage to the retina. And don't wait on warning signs: sudden vision changes, flashes, or eye pain deserve prompt attention from an eye-care professional.

related.title: Why Regular Checkups Matter
related.hook: The whole point of a checkup is to catch trouble while it's still quiet — before symptoms show up and while it's easiest to treat.

related.title: Preventing Type 2 Diabetes
related.hook: Type 2 diabetes often arrives slowly, with a warning stage called prediabetes — and at that stage, modest lifestyle changes can stop or delay it.

related.title: When a Symptom Needs a Doctor
related.hook: Most everyday symptoms pass on their own. The skill worth having is recognizing the red flags that mean don't wait — call for help now.

flashcards.prompt: Why are regular eye exams important even if your vision seems fine?
flashcards.back_html: Diseases like glaucoma can damage sight with no early symptoms, so a comprehensive exam may be the only way to catch them early enough to treat.

flashcards.prompt: What is the 20-20-20 rule for screen comfort?

choices.text: Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Work 20 hours, rest 20 minutes, 20 times a day
Sit 20 inches from the screen at all times

flashcards.explanation_html: The 20-20-20 habit gives your eyes a break from close focus: every 20 minutes, look about 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
